inline_comments.comment: Copy-paste bug: `node.width = 14` should be `node.height = 14`. The PR description explicitly claims this fixes the previous copy-paste bug, but the fix was not applied — `node.height` is still never set by this guard, so the node height remains `undefined`/falsy even after this block runs.
Same copy-paste bug as `stateEnd.ts`: `node.width = 14` should be `node.height = 14`. The `!node.height` guard silently leaves `node.height` unset.

The PR description states: 'barbNeo uses `transitionColor` from theme variables (not `archEdgeArrowColor`) so state diagrams use the correct semantic color.' The implementation does the opposite — it destructures and uses `archEdgeArrowColor`, which is intended for architecture diagrams. Replace with `transitionColor` to match the stated design decision and to correctly colour state-diagram arrows.

The shared `barb` marker's `refX` was changed from `19` to `14`. The PR description explicitly says 'The shared **`barb`** marker is unchanged (still `refX: 19`) so other diagram types are not affected.' This change silently alters arrowhead positioning for every diagram that uses `barb` (e.g. flowcharts, sequence diagrams), which is a breaking rendering regression unrelated to neo look. Revert this to `19` if the intent is to keep other diagrams unchanged.

`.attr('markerUnits', 'strokeWidth')` is set and then immediately overridden by `.attr('markerUnits', 'userSpaceOnUse')` on the very next chained call. The first assignment is dead code and should be removed. In D3, repeated `.attr()` calls with the same attribute name simply overwrite the previous value.

`configApi.getConfig()` is called directly inside `barbNeo`, an internal rendering-utility function. Project rules require that internal rendering helpers do not call `getConfig()` directly; instead they should receive an explicit `config: MermaidConfig` parameter threaded from the top-level entry point. This also introduces a hidden dependency that makes the function untestable in isolation. The import of `configApi` at the top of `markers.js` was added solely for this call and should be removed along with refactoring `barbNeo` to accept a `config` argument.

The width/height guard logic is redundant and hard to follow. The outer `if (node.width || node.height)` guard only runs the min-14 clamping when at least one dimension is truthy, then the subsequent `if (!node.width)` / `if (!node.height)` blocks run unconditionally to cover the all-zero case. This can be simplified to a single pass: `node.width = Math.max(node.width ?? 0, 14); node.height = Math.max(node.height ?? 0, 14);`. The same pattern exists in `stateStart.ts`.

`// @ts-ignore TODO: Fix typings` was added in this PR. Project convention requires `// @ts-expect-error: <descriptive reason>` instead of `// @ts-ignore`, so TypeScript will error if the suppression becomes unnecessary. Add a brief description of what the typing gap is (e.g. the specific roughjs call that lacks proper types) so it can be tracked and resolved.

The comment `.attr('refY', 5) // What!!!??` added inside `circleEnd-margin` is an unexplained, informal placeholder. It should either explain why the value is non-obvious or be removed. Comments of this form ('What!!!??') are not appropriate for production code.

`getConfig()` is called a second time here to read `config.look`. Earlier in the same function `conf` is obtained from `getConfig()` (or a similar call). Check whether `look` is already accessible via the existing `conf` variable or its parent. If not, capture both values in a single `getConfig()` call at the top of the function to avoid redundant work and stale-config risk.

The nested `for` loops that generate all pairwise transitions (O(n²) edges) produce very dense, fully-connected graphs (e.g. 10 transitions for 5 states). This makes the snapshots difficult to review visually and hard to reason about as a regression baseline. Consider replacing the dynamic generation with a small set of hand-written, representative diagram strings whose intent is immediately clear.

`imgSnapshotTest('info', ...)` inside a state-diagram spec renders an `info` diagram, not a state diagram. This is unrelated to the feature being tested and will produce a spurious snapshot. Move it to a generic or info-diagram spec, or replace it with a meaningful state-diagram test.

general_comments.comment: The PR description states that drop-shadow behaviour was refactored: 'Drop-shadow is driven by a **`nodeShadow` theme variable** instead of `theme?.includes("redux"`)'. The implementation still uses `theme?.includes('redux')` in both `stateStart.ts` and `stateEnd.ts`, and no theme file changes appear in the diff. Grepping the codebase shows `nodeShadow` has zero occurrences anywhere — the theme files were never updated. Either the description is aspirational and should be corrected, or the theme-variable approach still needs to be implemented to complete the stated design goal.

The Cypress spec generates test-case titles dynamically via `forEach` loops (e.g. `Test ${featureSet.name} in ${look} look and ${theme} theme - set ${setIndex + 1}`). Snapshot file names are derived from these titles; any future rename to make the titles clearer will orphan all existing baselines. Per project convention, snapshot test titles should be stable strings. Consider defining titles as constants or restructuring the loops to produce fixed `describe`/`it` strings.
